contentText:
The VELORA-301 Phase III trial has demonstrated that veloricept in combination with pembrolizumab significantly improves progression-free survival in patients with first-line advanced non-small cell lung cancer.

Key findings:
• Hazard ratio: 0.61 (95% CI 0.48–0.77; p<0.001)
• Median PFS: 14.2 months (veloricept arm) vs 8.7 months (pembrolizumab alone)
• Results were consistent across pre-specified subgroups

These data support the potential of veloricept as a clinically meaningful addition to the treatment landscape for advanced NSCLC. Full trial results are published in the New England Journal of Medicine.

VELORA-301 Phase III Primary PFS Data Summary

Population: Patients with untreated advanced NSCLC (n=487), ECOG PS 0–2, any PD-L1 expression.

Primary endpoint: Progression-free survival (investigator-assessed, RECIST v1.1).

Results: Median PFS 14.2 months (veloricept + pembrolizumab) vs 8.7 months (pembrolizumab + placebo). HR 0.61 (95% CI 0.48–0.77; p<0.001, pre-specified significance threshold p<0.01).

Subgroup consistency: Benefit observed across PD-L1 expression levels and histology subgroups. Interaction p-values non-significant.

Ref: VELORA-301 CSR v1.0 · Table 14.2.1 · Primary Analysis

Subject: VELORA-301 Phase III Primary PFS Results Now Available

Dear [HCP Name],

We are pleased to share that the primary efficacy results from the VELORA-301 Phase III trial are now available.

Veloricept plus pembrolizumab demonstrated a statistically significant improvement in progression-free survival (hazard ratio 0.61; 95% CI 0.48–0.77; p<0.001) versus pembrolizumab alone in patients with first-line advanced NSCLC.

Median PFS was 14.2 months in the combination arm versus 8.7 months in the control arm.

Full data including subgroup analyses and safety are available in the enclosed summary.

If you have questions, please contact your GenBioCa Medical Affairs representative.

Medical Affairs Team
GenBioCa Sciences

VELORA-301 Safety Profile — Grade 3+ TRAE Summary

Grade 3 or higher treatment-related adverse events (TRAEs) occurred in 52% of patients in the veloricept arm versus 44% in the pembrolizumab control arm.

No new safety signals were identified. The safety profile was consistent with the known profiles of each agent. Immune-mediated adverse events were manageable with standard protocols.

Common Grade 3+ TRAEs (≥5% in either arm): fatigue, decreased appetite, pneumonitis (veloricept arm: 8%), elevated ALT/AST.

Ref: VELORA-301 CSR v1.0 · Table 12.2.4 · Safety Population (n=487)

Medical Affairs Briefing Note — Veloricept Safety Profile

For internal Medical Affairs use only.

Key safety data from VELORA-301:
• Grade 3+ TRAE rate: 52% (veloricept arm) vs 44% (control)
• No new safety signals identified in the Phase III dataset
• Immune-mediated AEs: pneumonitis (8%), colitis (3%), endocrinopathies (6%)
• Treatment discontinuation due to AEs: 12% vs 8%

All safety data reviewed and accepted by PV Lead (Dr R. Morton, VELORA-301 Super Review, 15 Oct 2026).

For HCP communications, refer to approved SmPC §4.8 and approved label language only.

Consistent benefit across subgroups in VELORA-301: the PFS improvement with veloricept plus pembrolizumab was observed regardless of PD-L1 expression level and tumour histology (squamous and non-squamous), supporting a broad patient population.

Note: Claim currency flag acknowledged — PD-L1 subgroup language confirmed consistent with approved SmPC v1.0.

VELORA-301 Subgroup Analyses — Consistency Summary

PD-L1 Subgroups (CPS threshold):
• CPS ≥1%: HR 0.59 (95% CI 0.44–0.79)
• CPS ≥50%: HR 0.55 (95% CI 0.38–0.79)
• CPS <1%: HR 0.68 (95% CI 0.47–0.98)

Histology:
• Squamous: HR 0.59 (95% CI 0.42–0.83)
• Non-squamous: HR 0.62 (95% CI 0.46–0.83)

All interaction p-values non-significant. Benefit consistent across subgroups.

Claim currency note: PD-L1 subgroup language reviewed against SmPC v1.0 (approved). Confirmed current.

Ref: VELORA-301 CSR v1.0 · Table 14.2.7.1 and 14.2.7.2
